content.text:
Done. Admins can now pin the models used for background (non-explicit) LLM tasks from the models settings page, with automatic fallback and a UI warning when a pinned model becomes unavailable.

## What I built

**A "Default models" card** on the models page (`_sidebar-layout.settings.project.models.tsx`), below LLM Configuration. It offers exactly the two modes you asked for:
- **One default for everything** — a single dropdown applied to all background tasks.
- **A model per task** — one dropdown per category.

Categories (defined once in `apps/shared/src/background-models.ts` and reused everywhere):
- **Live story refresh** → `live-story.ts`
- **Title generation** → `automation-title.ts`
- **Conversation compaction** → `compaction.ts`
- **Context recommendations** → `context-recommendations.service.ts`
- **Other tasks** → `cron-nlp.ts` and memory extraction (`memory.ts`)

Each dropdown includes a **"nao default (automatic)"** option so any task can be left on the built-in per-provider default (`summaryModelId` / `extractorModelId` / `getDefaultModelId`), which is exactly today's behavior when nothing is configured.

**Fallback + warning behavior**: `resolveDefaultModelSelection(projectId, category)` in `utils/llm.ts` returns the pinned model only if it's still in the project's available models; if it was disabled/removed it substitutes another available model (same provider first, otherwise the first available one). The UI compares the stored selection against the available models and shows an amber warning icon + tooltip next to any task whose pinned model is gone, while the backend keeps running on a working model.

**Priority rules per task**: an explicitly passed selection (e.g. automation title, or the context-recommendations config's own model) always wins; then the admin's category/single default; then the built-in default. This is why context recommendations works "in both places" — its dedicated config model still takes precedence, and the new default is the next fallback.

## Storage & migrations
- New nullable JSON column `default_models` on the `project` table for both dialects.
- Generated `0059_add_project_default_models.sql` for `migrations-sqlite` and `migrations-postgres` (each a single clean `ADD COLUMN`); `db:check-migrations` passes.

## tRPC
- `project.getDefaultModels` → `{ settings, availableModels }`
- `project.updateDefaultModels` (admin-only)

I also updated the settings search index. `npm run lint` (tsc + eslint across backend/frontend/shared) passes clean.

One decision worth flagging: I folded **memory extraction** into the "Other" category alongside cron NLP, since it's the same kind of small background task — let me know if you'd rather leave memory on its per-chat model.

Per your team's testing preferences, I didn't do any visual/browser verification — I'll leave the UI walkthrough to you.
